gloss: tread; the way trodden: road, journey, manner, course of life
summary: דָּרַךְ is to tread: to set foot on land, to march, to trample, to tread grapes and olives in the press, and to tread a bow to string it; its hiphil is to make tread, to lead someone in a way (Isa 48:17). דֶּרֶךְ is the way trodden: a road, a journey along it (the ark went before Israel “a three days’ journey”, Num 10:33), a direction, a manner of going, and so the whole course of a life; “the way of Yahweh” is both the conduct he commands (Gen 18:19) and his own works and dealings (Psa 103:7). Phoenician drk “road” and Aramaic and Ugaritic drk “tread” share the meaning; in Arabic, Old South Arabian and the Peshitta the root is to reach, overtake and lay hold of.

words.gloss: way, road; journey; direction; manner; course of life, conduct
words.summary: The commonest word of the root, about 700 times: from the road underfoot it runs to a journey, a direction, a custom, a man’s conduct, and the ways of Yahweh, both those he commands and those he himself takes.

senses.definition: A way that is walked or driven along: a road between places, the road a traveller is on.

evidence.note: “We will go by the king’s דֶּרֶךְ; we will not turn to the right hand nor to the left.”
The ass sees the angel standing in the דֶּרֶךְ and turns aside out of the דֶּרֶךְ into the field.
The prophet’s body is thrown in the דֶּרֶךְ, and men passing by see it.
The spring on the דֶּרֶךְ to Shur.
Cursed is he who makes the blind wander out of the דֶּרֶךְ.
“When you walk by the דֶּרֶךְ”, beside sitting in the house.

“Prepare in the wilderness the דֶּרֶךְ of Yahweh; make straight in the desert a highway (מְסִלָּה) for our God”: a road made ready for his coming. Quoted of John the Baptist (Mat 3:3; Mrk 1:3; Luk 3:4; Jhn 1:23).
“My messenger shall clear the דֶּרֶךְ before me”; quoted Mat 11:10, Mrk 1:2, Luk 7:27.
“The דֶּרֶךְ of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations”, quoted Mat 4:15.
ὁδὸν θαλάσσης, from Isa 8:23.
The cherubim keep the דֶּרֶךְ of the tree of life.

senses.definition: A going from one place to another, and the distance it covers, reckoned in days.

evidence.note: Israel set out from the mountain of Yahweh “a דֶּרֶךְ of three days”, and the ark of the covenant of Yahweh went before them “a דֶּרֶךְ of three days” to search out a resting place for them.
Laban set “a דֶּרֶךְ of three days” between himself and Jacob.
A man unclean, “or on a far דֶּרֶךְ”, keeps the Passover in the second month; Num 9:13 sets him beside the man who is clean and “not on a דֶּרֶךְ”.
“Let us go a דֶּרֶךְ of three days into the wilderness, and sacrifice to Yahweh.”
Whether Yahweh had made his דֶּרֶךְ prosper.
Provision for the דֶּרֶךְ.
Clothes and shoes worn out “by reason of the very long דֶּרֶךְ”.
A fast, to seek of God “a straight דֶּרֶךְ for us”.

senses.definition: The way a thing faces or a person looks or goes; before a place name or a quarter it comes close to “toward”.

evidence.note: “Lift up your eyes the דֶּרֶךְ of the north”, and he lifted his eyes the דֶּרֶךְ of the north.
Captives who pray “the דֶּרֶךְ of their land … the city you have chosen and the house I have built”: toward them.
Beyond the Jordan, behind the דֶּרֶךְ of the going down of the sun.
The gate whose face is the דֶּרֶךְ of the east, and the glory of the God of Israel coming from the דֶּרֶךְ of the east.
In by the gate the דֶּרֶךְ of the north, out by the gate the דֶּרֶךְ of the south.

senses.definition: The way a thing commonly goes: the manner of a creature or a people, a custom, the common lot.

evidence.note: “There is no man in the earth to come in to us after the דֶּרֶךְ of all the earth.”
“The דֶּרֶךְ of women is upon me.”
The דֶּרֶךְ of an eagle in the air, of a serpent on a rock, of a ship in the sea, and of a man with a young woman: how each goes, which leaves no track.
“I go the דֶּרֶךְ of all the earth”: David near death; also Jos 23:14.
Pestilence “after the דֶּרֶךְ of Egypt”; also Isa 10:24, 26.
“Learn not the דֶּרֶךְ of the nations.”

senses.definition: The way a person goes through life: what he does and how he lives, good or evil, which God sees and judges.

evidence.note: “All flesh had corrupted its דֶּרֶךְ upon the earth.”
“To give every man according to his דְּרָכִים, according to the fruit of his doings (מַעֲלָלָיו).”
Israel defiled the land “by their דֶּרֶךְ and by their doings (עֲלִילוֹתָם)”.
God saw their works, that they turned from their evil דֶּרֶךְ.
“Yahweh knows the דֶּרֶךְ of the righteous, but the דֶּרֶךְ of the wicked shall perish.”
To bring his דֶּרֶךְ upon his head: the consequence of what he did.
“There is a דֶּרֶךְ that seems right to a man, but its end is the ways of death”; also Pro 16:25.
“The דֶּרֶךְ of man is not in himself; it is not in man who walks to direct his steps.”
“We have turned every one to his own דֶּרֶךְ, and Yahweh has laid on him the iniquity of us all.”
“Set your heart upon your דְּרָכִים.”
“Let us search and try our דְּרָכִים, and return to Yahweh.”
He walked in the דֶּרֶךְ of his father: a king’s conduct followed by his son.
The angel to Balaam: “your דֶּרֶךְ is headlong before me”; 2Pe 2:15 calls it “the way of Balaam”.
They have followed the ὁδός of Balaam, who loved the wages of unrighteousness.
“The דֶּרֶךְ of peace they do not know”, quoted Rom 3:17.

senses.definition: The conduct Yahweh requires and teaches: walking in his ways is keeping his commandments, doing righteousness and judgment.

evidence.note: Abraham will command his children “and they shall keep the דֶּרֶךְ of Yahweh, to do righteousness and judgment”.
“To walk in his דְּרָכִים, to keep his statutes, his commandments, his judgments and his testimonies.”
“Blessed are the blameless in the דֶּרֶךְ, who walk in the law of Yahweh.”
“They do not know the דֶּרֶךְ of Yahweh, the judgment of their God”, in parallel.
“They have turned aside quickly out of the דֶּרֶךְ which I commanded them; they have made a calf.”
Walk in all the דֶּרֶךְ Yahweh your God commanded you, that you may live.
To love Yahweh, to walk in his דְּרָכִים and keep his commandments, that you may live.
“He will teach us of his דְּרָכִים and we will walk in his paths, for out of Zion shall go forth the law”; also Mic 4:2.
“Make me know your דְּרָכִים, Yahweh; teach me your paths.”
“Ask for the old paths, where the good דֶּרֶךְ is, and walk in it, and you shall find rest for your souls.”
“I set before you the דֶּרֶךְ of life and the דֶּרֶךְ of death.”
“The דְּרָכִים of Yahweh are right; the righteous walk in them, but transgressors stumble in them.”
Paul to Elymas: “will you not cease to pervert the right ὁδοί of the Lord?”, the words of Hos 14:10.
The priests “have turned aside out of the דֶּרֶךְ”.

senses.gloss: Yahweh’s own ways, his works and dealings
senses.definition: What Yahweh himself does: his works in creation and his dealings with men, which are higher than man’s.

evidence.note: “He made known his דְּרָכִים to Moses, his deeds (עֲלִילוֹתָיו) to the children of Israel.”
“Yahweh possessed me the beginning of his דֶּרֶךְ, before his works (מִפְעָלָיו) of old.”
After his works in the heavens and the sea: “Lo, these are the edges of his דְּרָכִים.”
“They have not known my דְּרָכִים”; Heb 3:9–10 sets it beside “they saw my works forty years”.
Behemoth is “the first of the דַּרְכֵי of God”: of his works in creation.
“Neither are your ways my דְּרָכִים … as the heavens are higher than the earth.”
“All his דְּרָכִים are judgment.”
Righteous in all his דְּרָכִים, holy in all his works.
“Is not my דֶּרֶךְ equal? Are not your ways unequal?”
“Yahweh has his דֶּרֶךְ in the whirlwind and in the storm.”

senses.definition: In two verses the parallel sets דֶּרֶךְ beside strength and warriors. Whether it means power there, as Ugaritic drkt “rule”, or a man’s course and dealings, the verses leave open.

evidence.note: “Give not your strength (חֵילְךָ) to women, nor your דְּרָכִים to what destroys kings.”
“You trusted in your דֶּרֶךְ, in the multitude of your mighty men.”

senses.definition: To put one’s foot on ground or on a thing: to walk upon it, and of land, to come into it and so take it.

evidence.note: “Every place on which the sole of your foot treads shall be yours.”
“The land on which your foot has trodden shall be your inheritance”, Moses’ oath to Caleb; also Deu 1:36.
The priests of Dagon do not tread on the threshold of Dagon.
God alone spreads out the heavens “and treads upon the waves of the sea”.
“You trod the sea with your horses.”
Yahweh comes out of his place, comes down and treads upon the high places of the earth; also Amo 4:13.
The old path which wicked men have trodden.
Whoever treads on their crooked paths does not know peace.

senses.definition: To stride out, of a warrior, an army or a king coming forth.

evidence.note: “March on, my soul, with strength!”
“A star has trodden forth out of Jacob, and a sceptre has risen out of Israel”, in parallel with קָם “rise”.
When the Assyrian comes into our land and treads in our palaces, within our border.

senses.definition: To tread enemies underfoot in victory or wrath.

evidence.note: “Your enemies shall cringe before you, and you shall tread upon their high places.”
“You shall tread upon the lion and the adder”, in parallel with רָמַס “trample”.
“I trod them in my anger and trampled (וְאֶרְמְסֵם) them in my fury.”
“The Lord has trodden the virgin daughter of Judah as a winepress.”

senses.definition: To tread grapes in the winepress, or olives for oil, with the shouting of the vintage.

evidence.note: “The treader shall tread out no wine in the presses.”
“You shall tread the olive, but not anoint yourself with oil.”
Men treading winepresses on the sabbath.
They gathered their vineyards and trod.
Yahweh shouts “like those who tread” against all the inhabitants of the earth.
“Your garments like one who treads in the winepress.”
The treader of grapes shall overtake the sower.

senses.gloss: tread a bow, string or bend it
senses.definition: To tread on a bow to bend and string it, ready to shoot; of arrows, to aim them. The passive participle is “bent, strung”.

evidence.note: “The wicked tread the bow; they set their arrow on the string.”
“The wicked have drawn out the sword and trodden their bow.”
“Whose arrows are sharp and all their bows trodden (דְּרֻכוֹת)”; also Isa 21:15.
“He has trodden his bow like an enemy”; also Lam 3:12.
“I have trodden Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim.”
They tread their arrows, a bitter word.
“Treaders of the bow”: archers; also 1Ch 8:40; 2Ch 14:7.

evidence.note: “I am Yahweh your God, who teaches you to profit, who makes you tread in the דֶּרֶךְ you should go.”
“I have taught you in the דֶּרֶךְ of wisdom; I have made you tread in right paths.”
“He makes the humble tread in judgment, and teaches the humble his דֶּרֶךְ.”
“He made them tread in a straight דֶּרֶךְ, to go to a city to dwell in.”
“I will bring the blind by a way they did not know; in paths they have not known I will make them tread.”
“Make me tread in your truth and teach me.”
“Make me tread in the path of your commandments.”
“He makes me tread upon my high places.”
Yahweh strikes the River into seven streams “and makes men tread it in sandals”.

senses.definition: To tread down, of an enemy overrun, of grain on the threshing floor, and of ground trodden.

evidence.note: They pursued Benjamin and trod him down.

The path to wisdom: the proud beasts have not trodden it.

words.gloss: (aphel) overtake, come upon; attain, lay hold of; perceive, comprehend
words.summary: The Peshitta has the root only in the aphel, never for “tread” or “way” (its way is ܐܘܪܚܐ): it renders καταλαμβάνω, and also φθάνω and ἐπιλαμβάνομαι. This is the sense of Arabic adraka and Old South Arabian drk, to reach and overtake, which the Hebrew does not show; how it joins “tread” is not clear, unless it is coming up with someone step by step.

stems.gloss: overtake; attain, lay hold of; perceive

Festus found that he had done nothing worthy of death.

cognates.gloss: tread, step on; (aphel) lead; trace, overtake; thresh
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic: the Targums use it for Hebrew דָּרַךְ “tread” (Onkelos Deu 1:36; Targ. Isa 59:8), and its aphel for “lead” (Targ. Prov 22:6; Targ. Psa 25:9), answering to the Hebrew hiphil; it also has “overtake” as in Syriac.

evidence.note: “same [to tread]. Targ. O. Deut. I, 36. Targ. Is. LIX, 8 … Af. 1) to lead. Targ. Prov. XXII, 6 … Targ. Ps. XXV, 9 … 2) to trace, overtake.”

cognates.gloss: reach, overtake, come up with; attain; perceive, comprehend
cognates.note: Lane’s sources give form IV “he, or it, attained, reached, overtook, or came up with, him, or it … I walked until I overtook him”, hence “attained, obtained” and “perceived it; attained a knowledge of it”; the noun darak is “the act of attaining, reaching, or overtaking”. The first form is unused. This is exactly the Peshitta’s aphel (overtake, lay hold of, comprehend); the Hebrew does not use the root so.
Sabaean inscriptions: ydrkhmw “they overtook them on the night of the next day”; hdrkhmw b-ʾṯrhmw “they pursued after them”. The sense of Arabic adraka and the Peshitta’s aphel.

evidence.note: “vb … OVERTAKE by pursuit”; “h … (1) PURSUE … (2) OVERTAKE”.

doctrine.statement: Yahweh charged Abraham’s house to “keep the way of Yahweh, to do righteousness and judgment” (Gen 18:19), and set before Israel, and later Jerusalem, two ways: “the way of life and the way of death” (Deu 30:15–16; Jer 21:8). Psalm 1 ends with the same two: Yahweh knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked shall perish (Psa 1:6); and “there is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the ways of death” (Pro 14:12). Jesus speaks of a broad way to destruction and a narrow way to life (Mat 7:13–14), says “I am the way, the truth and the life: no man comes to the Father but by me” (Jhn 14:6), and his first followers were called those “of the Way” (Act 9:2; 19:9, 23; 24:14, 22); Hebrews calls the entry into the holy place by his blood “a new and living way” (Heb 10:19–20). From the verses: the way of Yahweh was always a way to walk, conduct leading to life, and the New Testament finds it in Jesus himself, so that following him is walking in it.

Isaiah’s voice cries, “Prepare in the wilderness the way of Yahweh … behold your God” (Isa 40:3, 9), and Malachi’s messenger clears the way before Yahweh, after whom “the Lord whom you seek shall suddenly come to his temple” (Mal 3:1). All four Gospels apply these to John the Baptist preparing the way before Jesus (Mat 3:3; 11:10; Mrk 1:2–3; Luk 1:76; 3:4; Jhn 1:23). Jesus said he came in his Father’s name (Jhn 5:43), and Paul that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself (2Co 5:19). From the verses: the coming of Yahweh for which the way was prepared took place in his Son, in whom the Father was at work.

In Proverbs, wisdom speaks as a woman calling at the gates (Pro 8:1–3; 9:1–3), and says, “Yahweh possessed me the beginning of his way, before his works of old” (Pro 8:22). Here his way is his working, set beside his works, as behemoth is “the first of the ways of God” (Job 40:19) and his ways are his deeds (Psa 103:7). Wisdom was beside him when he set the heavens and marked out the foundations of the earth (Pro 8:27–30), as “Yahweh by wisdom founded the earth” (Pro 3:19). Paul writes that Christ is “the wisdom of God”, made to us wisdom from God, and that in him are hid all the treasures of wisdom (1Co 1:24, 30; Col 2:3). From the verses: Pro 8:22 personifies Yahweh’s own wisdom, present at the start of his works; it does not speak of a second person existing beside him, and the New Testament finds that wisdom shown in Christ.

Yahweh promised Israel “every place on which the sole of your foot treads” (Deu 11:24; Jos 1:3), and swore to Caleb that the land his foot had trodden would be his inheritance for ever (Jos 14:9). Of Esau’s land he would not give Israel “a treading of the sole of a foot” (Deu 2:5). Stephen uses those words of Abraham: God “gave him no inheritance in it, not even a footstep, yet promised to give it to him for a possession, and to his seed after him” (Act 7:5; Gen 13:15). Hebrews says Abraham and the fathers “died in faith, not having received the promises”, and that they will not be made perfect without us (Heb 11:8–13, 39–40). From the verses: the land promised to Abraham himself was never trodden as his own in his life, so the promise waits for the resurrection, when he receives it with his seed.

Yahweh, asked why his garments are red “like one who treads in the winepress”, answers, “I have trodden the winepress alone … I trod them in my anger and trampled them in my fury” (Isa 63:1–6); he had trodden Judah too “as a winepress” (Lam 1:15). In Revelation the vine of the earth is cast into “the great winepress of the wrath of God”, trodden outside the city (Rev 14:19–20), and the rider called the Word of God, his garment dipped in blood, “treads the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of God Almighty” (Rev 19:13, 15). From the verses: the judgment Yahweh carries out alone in Isaiah is carried out by Christ at his return, when he judges the nations.

Job says of God that he alone “spreads out the heavens and treads upon the waves of the sea” (Job 9:8), and Habakkuk that Yahweh trod the sea with his horses (Hab 3:15). Jesus came to his disciples walking on the sea (Mat 14:25; Mrk 6:48; Jhn 6:19), and said of his works, “the Father who dwells in me, he does the works” (Jhn 14:10). From the verses: what Job ascribes to God alone, Jesus did, and he gave the work to the Father dwelling in him.

Balaam sees one “not now … not near”: “a star has trodden forth out of Jacob, and a sceptre has risen out of Israel, and shall strike the corners of Moab”, with Edom his possession (Num 24:17–18). David struck Moab and made Edom his servants (2Sa 8:2, 14), and Jesus calls himself “the root and the offspring of David, the bright and morning star” (Rev 22:16). From the verses: the star is a king of Jacob’s line who conquers Israel’s neighbours; David’s victories were a first showing, and Jesus, David’s son, takes the title as his own.

note: Left out: דַּרְכְּמוֹן / אֲדַרְכּוֹן (d.ci.ad, a.bf.aj; Ezr 2:69; 8:27; Neh 7:69–71; 1Ch 29:7), the daric or drachma, a coin name from Persian (and/or Greek δραχμή), not of this root; it belongs in an entry of its own as a loan. BDB’s m.am.az for מִדְרָךְ is a cross-reference with no tokens; d.ci.ac counts the word. Not yet followed: Ge'ez daraka “be harsh, severe” (lead in Fisher p. 69, dillmann-1865/leslau-1987 not consulted), which would count against the root if confirmed; Arabic darak “a stage downward; the lowest depth” (Lane p. 874) as a possible link to מִדְרָךְ; Ugaritic drk the verb in a glossary with texts (only Anderson–Moser so far). The Syriac nouns are glossed from SEDRA (lexemes 757, 759) with one verse each. Num 10:33 is the verse that prompted the entry (Numbers 10).
